title: GuardMem AI
tagline: A memory governance gateway for long-running AI agents
overview: Every candidate fact an agent wants to remember is intercepted before it becomes durable state. GuardMem extracts structured claims anchored to verbatim source spans, validates them against a tenant ontology, scores confidence and blast-radius risk on separate axes, and then auto-writes, queues for human review, rejects, or escalates. Every decision lands in a hash-chained audit log.
challenges: Stopping confabulation at the door: no verbatim source span, no write.
Separating confidence (semantic entropy over meaning clusters) from impact risk (blast radius) so a confident write to a high-stakes field still escalates.
Fail-closed degradation: provider outage, budget cap or injection detection all route toward human review and never widen the auto-write path.
Never deleting beliefs: supersession plus tombstones with bitemporal columns make 'what did the agent believe on date X' a normal query.
architecture:
raw turns
   |
   v
[L1 EXTRACTION]  noise -> candidates + verbatim spans
   |
   v
[L2 VALIDATION]  ontology | NLI contradiction | cardinality | temporal overlap
   |
   v
[L3 SCORING]     C (semantic entropy)   R (blast radius)
   |
   v
[DECISION] --> AUTO_WRITE | HITL_REVIEW | REJECT | ESCALATE
   |
   v
Postgres txn + hash-chained audit events

title: Resident OS
tagline: AI operations layer for apartment communities, starting with maintenance
overview: A resident report becomes a safe, cited, policy-checked, human-reviewable dispatch decision with an immutable audit trail. It sits alongside property-management systems such as Yardi and Entrata. The model proposes; deterministic code validates and authorises, and only the orchestrator holds side-effecting tool authority.
challenges: Deterministic life-safety screening that never depends on a model deciding whether to notify a person.
Tenant isolation through row-level security plus an explicit organisation predicate on keyset-paginated queries.
Extractive compression that keeps verbatim source sentences with offsets, so lease and safety language is never summarised.
Token-budgeted context assembly with deterministic [C#] citations and [F#] facts.

Resident report
   |
   v
[Intake + life-safety screen]  (deterministic)
   |
   v
[Hybrid retrieval] BM25 + pgvector --RRF--> cross-encoder rerank
   |
   v
[Context assembly] [C#] cites | [F#] facts | 8k budget
   |
   v
[Decision proposal] --> [Policy audit] --> [Human approval]
   |
   v
Dispatch proposal + immutable audit trace

title: Enterprise HR Agentic RAG Copilot
tagline: Agentic RAG that grades its evidence, or refuses to answer
overview: A Forward Deployed Engineer style project that takes a RAG notebook to a deployable internal HR product. An 11-node LangGraph agent routes, grades retrieved evidence, rewrites queries, falls back to cited web search, and finally declines. Every answer is logged to an audit trail the browser console renders.
challenges: Making 'internal policy does not cover this' a reachable outcome, not a fallback nobody wired up.
Calibrating the 0.15 relevance gate from a 12-question benchmark so it rejects every out-of-domain chunk and drops no real one.
Multi-format ingestion (Markdown, TXT, PDF, DOCX with tables) with deterministic chunk IDs and orphan pruning.
Auditable answers without leaking employee questions to third parties; tracing is redacted by default.

title: Latent Instability Diagnostics (LID)
tagline: Detect LLM hallucinations one token before they are emitted
overview: Every mainstream hallucination detector is post-hoc. LID measures how sensitive a model's hidden-state manifold is to controlled Gaussian perturbation, flagging a tipping point 1 to 2 tokens ahead of the first hallucinated token. Eight baselines are reproduced behind a unified API for a fair comparison.
challenges: Formalising instability as I(l,t) magnitude divergence plus q(l,t) directional alignment, combined into a composite score Z.
Keeping cost to 15-20% on one consumer GPU by re-projecting perturbed states through a stateless lm_head with 8-bit per-token tracing.
Reproducing DoLa, Semantic Entropy, LSD, SSP, INSIDE, SEP and ITI under one harness.
Making every figure regenerable by one command behind a 1,250-line pytest suite.
architecture:
prompt -> LLM decode step t
            |
            v
   hidden state h_l(t)
      |            \
      |   + Gaussian noise (sigma = alpha * RMS(h))
      v            v
   h_clean       h_pert
        \          /
   I = ||dh|| / ||h||    q = cos(h_clean, h_pert)
               |
               v
      Z = w*I + (1-w)*(1-q)
               |
   peak > mean(Z) + 1.5*std(Z)  -->  flag BEFORE token t+1

title: Maryland UI Pulse
tagline: Are Maryland's unemployed paid within 21 days? A live US map, benchmark and forecast
overview: An independent analytics project on how quickly Maryland pays first unemployment insurance benefits, benchmarked against every US jurisdiction using public US Department of Labor data. It ships as a live interactive web app with a state map, trend explorer, delay distribution, claims forecast and what-if slider, plus a Power BI report, static dashboards and a Q&A. Maryland pays 72.5% of first payments within 21 days against an 87% federal standard, 48th of 53.
challenges: Working out an undocumented federal file: the ETA 9050 column layout had to be inferred, and an early double-count was caught by checking against the Department's own published chart (Maryland 69.3% and US 83.4% for 2025, 14.1% in June 2020).
Separating volume from lateness: late payments average about 1,600 a month whether claims rise or fall (correlation 0.01), which points to process bottlenecks rather than intake capacity.
Being honest about what public data cannot show: backdating cannot be separated from agency delay, correlations are descriptive, and the forecast is illustrative.

One pipeline, several audiences: a live web app, a Power BI project and .pbix, static dashboards and state maps, all rebuilt from two public files, with a tone that treats the Department's challenges as context, not blame.
architecture:
US DOL ETA 9050 + ETA 539 (public CSVs)
   |
   v
[Python pipeline] pandas -> clean datasets, checked against MD Labor's own published chart
   |

   |
   +--> [Plotly] US and Mid-Atlantic state maps
   |
   +--> [Power BI project] TMDL model + DAX + 3-page report (.pbix)
   |

[Web app] d3 map + Chart.js, static site on Vercel (auto-deploys on push)

title: Fashion Image Caption Generator
tagline: 48M-parameter captioner that beats larger zero-shot VLMs on garment attributes
overview: A CNN-Transformer encoder-decoder trained from scratch on 45K Myntra fashion images, compared against Qwen2-VL and BLIP-2. A Streamlit dashboard offers caption generation, token-level importance and side-by-side model comparison.
challenges: Outperforming zero-shot Qwen2-VL-2B and BLIP-2 on catalogue-style attributes with 18x fewer parameters.
Migrating inference from a per-image generate loop to vLLM with continuous batching and prefix caching.
Validating grounding with decoder cross-attention rollout: 63% region agreement on 80 hand-annotated images.
Building an error taxonomy from 120 human preference judgments across 3 reviewers.

title: WillDocs RAG
tagline: Streaming chat over your PDFs with hybrid search and reranking
overview: A full-stack local RAG system built from scratch with LlamaIndex, Qdrant, FastAPI, Streamlit and Docker. Dense-only search was replaced with BM25-dense fusion via RRF, then reranked with a MiniLM cross-encoder. An embedding-keyed semantic cache trims cost per query.
challenges: Serving 3,400 chunks from 120 mixed-format documents under 5 concurrent users on a shared CPU.
Hybrid BM25-dense retrieval fused with RRF, reranking top 12 down to 4.
Streaming answers over async FastAPI and server-sent events.
architecture:
PDFs -> parse -> chunk -> embed -> Qdrant

query
   |
   +--> BM25 ----+
   |             +--RRF--> top 12 --> cross-encoder --> top 4
   +--> dense ---+                                      |
   |                                                    v
   +--> semantic cache (hit: skip LLM)         LLM --SSE--> Streamlit

title: Human-Gated External Memory (HGEM)
tagline: Does unfiltered memory cause reasoning drift in LLM agents?
overview: A research programme testing whether restricting long-term memory to human-validated reasoning states lowers Constraint Violation Rate and Reasoning Drift Index. Memory is split into immutable laws, human-gated graph nodes and a five-turn ephemeral window, with random-gate and adversarial ablations.
status: Setup and dataset pipeline complete; experiments not started
challenges: Designing a 2x2 ablation that separates storage structure from human gating.
A shadow-model protocol that compares HGEM against full-history memory step by step.
An adversarial false-memory condition testing whether immutable T1 constants hold.
architecture:
context injection order

[T1 immutable constants]  locked, model cannot edit
          |
          v
[T2 Neo4j graph traversal]  human-approved nodes + dependency edges
          |
          v
[T3 last five turns]  ephemeral
          |
          v
        LLM   (never sees raw full history)
